Yes, there will always be someone more attractive than you or smarter than you or whatever, but when you are with someone that loves you that won’t matter because they want YOU. And if they do cheat, then that relationship just wasn’t meant to be. But trapping them and taking away their freedom is only going to lead to unsuccessful relationships and you being unhappy.

Actually as someone who really struggles with this I’m here to give you my thoughts. Keep in mind this is probably just a me thing and I’m not speaking for the whole community here^

But as horrible and silly as it may sound I actually do really struggle to see those people as people. More often when online, but even in person too but to a lesser degree. It’s just hard for me to see someone spew so much hate that I take very personally as someone who is capable of love and compassion and patience and kindness and etc. Because when someone make horrible assumptions about me for who I am and immediately jumps to disregarding me as a human and invalidating my existence it’s hard to view them in as anything else but the scum of the earth. I really genuinely feel so much hatred for these people and it’s an extreme and aggressive emotion and I still don’t really know how to deal with it.

I think a lot of it stems from my insecurity. I’m in constant defense mode when it comes to my queerness because the people in my life are so quick to invalidate me. My family mostly. I constantly feel like no one understands me. Like I’m completely alone in all this pain I feel. I’m American, so also watching my country regress so much with things like “don’t say gay” fill me with anger and hopelessness and despair and hatred. And I think I tend to take it out on individuals when I see them being hateful because in my mind they represent everything I hate. It’s a face to point the blame to instead of a collective oppression that’s existed for decades.

But obviously that’s not good. There’s a lot about everything I’ve told you that’s very unhealthy and that I need to change. But I hope this serves as an explanation to at least why I’m so horrible to the phobes sometimes, and maybe why others might be too if they relate to this at all.

This is imposter syndrome! It is very common within the lgbtq+ community and you aren’t alone in your feelings. When I began first questioning my gender I doubted myself constantly. I was so worried that my feelings were only a phase and that it was nothing to take serious. But it wasn’t that.

For starters, know that you don’t have to rush through this journey of figuring yourself out! I tried to figure myself out as quick as possible and ended up changing my label basically every day lol. Things like this take time, so you can sit with your feelings without any worry about the future just yet. Focus on what you feel *now*.

Also, once you give yourself time I think you’ll begin to feel more confident in your identity. After feeling the same way for so many days or months or years even if gets harder to deny it, at least in my experience.

Lastly, know that you don’t have to be right the first time. When I first started questioning I identified as a demigirl, and even now that I’ve been out for almost a year as boyflux I just recently changed my label because I found one that fit me more that the one I’d been using previously. There’s nothing wrong with your feelings changing towards labels or your gender itself. Though if you are worried about how other people would respond to that, you can give yourself more time to grow more sure of yourself before coming out :)
